```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6, fig.height = 6)
```

PrecFact fits the Bayesian precision factor model of Chandra, Müller and Sarkar (2026,
*Bayesian Analysis* 21(1), 75–103, doi:10.1214/24-BA1461). The precision matrix is written
as $\Omega = \Lambda\Lambda^T + \Delta$, with a $d \times q$ loading matrix $\Lambda$ and a
diagonal $\Delta$, and the conditional independence graph is selected by controlling the
posterior false discovery rate.

This vignette reproduces the simulated example of the original package at a smaller size,
so that it builds in a few seconds.

```{r}
library(PrecFact)
sim <- simulate_precfact(n = 200, d = 40, q = 4, pr = 0.1, val = 2.5, seed = 1)
```

`precfact()` centres and scales the data, chooses $q$ from a PCA of the data, runs the
Gibbs sampler and selects the graph. The article runs 5,500 iterations with 1,250 burn-in;
we use fewer here.

```{r}
fit <- precfact(sim$y, nrun = 2000, burn = 500, seed = 1, verbose = FALSE)
fit
summary(fit, top = 5)
```

Compare the true and estimated partial correlation matrices.

```{r, fig.height = 4}
truth <- sim$pcor; diag(truth) <- NA; truth[truth == 0] <- NA
est <- graph_pcor(fit); diag(est) <- NA; est[est == 0] <- NA

if (requireNamespace("patchwork", quietly = TRUE)) {
  patchwork::wrap_plots(heatplot(truth, diverging = TRUE) + ggplot2::ggtitle("True"),
                        heatplot(est, diverging = TRUE) + ggplot2::ggtitle("Estimated"))
}
```

The estimated network:

```{r}
plot_network(fit, title = "Estimated graph")
```

The posterior FDR across the grid of interval nulls, and a trace of $\log\det\Omega$:

```{r, fig.height = 3}
fit$fdr_table
plot_trace(fit)
```
